Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১) Severe, constant upper abdominal pain of increasing intensity over 15-60 minutes which radiates to the back is the typical presentation of
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Acute pancreatitis classically presents with severe, constant epigastric (upper abdominal) pain that gradually increases in intensity over 15–60 minutes and radiates to the back.

The pain occurs due to pancreatic inflammation and activation of digestive enzymes causing irritation of surrounding tissues. It is often associated with nausea, vomiting, and elevated serum lipase/amylase levels.

Exam pearl:
Severe epigastric pain radiating to the back → Acute pancreatitis
Pain relieved by leaning forward → Pancreatic pain
Most specific enzyme → Serum lipase

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২) Which modulates satiety?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
GLP-1 (Glucagon-like peptide-1) is an important hormone that modulates satiety by acting on the hypothalamus and reducing food intake.

Functions of GLP-1:

  • Increases satiety and decreases appetite

  • Stimulates glucose-dependent insulin secretion

  • Inhibits glucagon secretion

  • Delays gastric emptying

Exam pearl:
Satiety hormones → GLP-1, Peptide YY, CCK, Leptin
GLP-1 → Incretin hormone + satiety + ↑ insulin

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩) Which hepatitis virus cannont be prevented by vaccine
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Hepatitis C virus (HCV) currently has no effective vaccine because of its high genetic variability and rapid mutation.

  • Hepatitis A → Vaccine available

  • Hepatitis B → Vaccine available

  • Hepatitis D → No specific vaccine, but prevented indirectly by Hepatitis B vaccination since HDV requires HBV for infection.

Exam pearl:
No vaccine → Hepatitis C
HBV vaccine also protects against Hepatitis D

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪) Most common cause of acute pancreatitis
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Gallstones are the most common cause of acute pancreatitis worldwide. A gallstone may temporarily obstruct the ampulla of Vater, causing reflux and activation of pancreatic enzymes within the pancreas, leading to inflammation.

Exam pearl:
Most common cause of acute pancreatitis → Gallstones
Second most common cause → Alcohol

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৫) Which hepatitis virus doesn't develop chronicity?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Hepatitis A virus (HAV) causes acute hepatitis only and does not progress to chronic hepatitis. Infection usually resolves completely with lifelong immunity.

Exam pearl:

  • No chronicity → Hepatitis A & E

  • Chronic hepatitis → Hepatitis B, C, and D

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৬) Dyspepsia in patients over 55 or with alarm symptoms demands
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
In patients with dyspepsia who are >55 years old or who have alarm symptoms (e.g., weight loss, dysphagia, GI bleeding, anemia, persistent vomiting, family history of upper GI cancer), the recommended investigation is upper gastrointestinal endoscopy (esophagogastroduodenoscopy, EGD) to exclude malignancy and other serious pathology.

Exam pearl:
Age >55 years + alarm features in dyspepsia → Upper GI endoscopy is mandatory.


সলভ ক্লাসের জন্য আলোচনা পোস্ট দেখুন - [আলোচনা পোস্টের লিঙ্ক]

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৭) Structures that can be seen in upper GI endoscopy except
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Upper GI endoscopy (esophagogastroduodenoscopy, EGD) is primarily performed to examine the esophagus, stomach, and duodenum (including the first and usually the second part of the duodenum). Although the endoscope passes through the pharynx during insertion, the pharynx is not considered a structure examined as part of upper GI endoscopy.

Exam pearl:
Upper GI endoscopy visualizes → Esophagus → Stomach → 1st & 2nd part of duodenum.


সলভ ক্লাসের জন্য আলোচনা পোস্ট দেখুন - [আলোচনা পোস্টের লিঙ্ক]

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৮) Which can confirm acute pancreatitis?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Serum lipase is the most specific laboratory test for confirming acute pancreatitis. It rises within 4–8 hours, peaks at about 24 hours, and remains elevated for 8–14 days, making it more useful than amylase.

Exam pearl:
Acute pancreatitis → Serum lipase is the most specific diagnostic enzyme.
Diagnosis requires at least 2 of 3: typical abdominal pain, serum lipase/amylase ≥3× normal, or characteristic imaging findings.


সলভ ক্লাসের জন্য আলোচনা পোস্ট দেখুন - [আলোচনা পোস্টের লিঙ্ক]

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৯) Most common cause of acute upper gastrointestinal haemorrhage
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Peptic ulcer disease is the most common cause of acute upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage. Bleeding occurs due to erosion of an artery by a gastric or duodenal ulcer.

Exam pearl:
Most common cause of acute upper GI bleeding → Peptic ulcer disease
Most common cause of lower GI bleeding → Diverticular disease (adults)

সলভ ক্লাসের জন্য আলোচনা পোস্ট দেখুন - [আলোচনা পোস্টের লিঙ্ক]

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১০) Complicatiion that can arise from both acute and chronic pancreatitis
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Pancreatic pseudocyst is a recognized complication of both acute and chronic pancreatitis. It is a collection of pancreatic fluid surrounded by a fibrous wall without an epithelial lining, usually developing several weeks after pancreatic inflammation.

Exam pearl:
Complication common to both acute & chronic pancreatitis → Pancreatic pseudocyst
Pseudocyst = No epithelial lining (distinguishes it from a true cyst).


সলভ ক্লাসের জন্য আলোচনা পোস্ট দেখুন - [আলোচনা পোস্টের লিঙ্ক]

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১১) Faecal calprotectin is tested to detect
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Faecal calprotectin is a marker of intestinal mucosal inflammation. It is released from neutrophils and is elevated in inflammatory bowel diseases (IBD) such as Crohn's disease and ulcerative colitis. It helps differentiate IBD from irritable bowel syndrome (IBS).

Exam pearl:
↑ Faecal calprotectin → Intestinal mucosal inflammation (IBD)
Normal faecal calprotectin → Suggests IBS rather than IBD.


সলভ ক্লাসের জন্য আলোচনা পোস্ট দেখুন - [আলোচনা পোস্টের লিঙ্ক]

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১২) Steatorrhoea signify malabsorption of
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Steatorrhoea is the passage of bulky, pale, greasy, foul-smelling stools due to fat malabsorption. It occurs when digestion or absorption of dietary fat is impaired, as seen in chronic pancreatitis, celiac disease, and biliary obstruction.

Exam pearl:
Steatorrhoea = Fat malabsorption
Common causes → Chronic pancreatitis, Celiac disease, Bile salt deficiency

সলভ ক্লাসের জন্য আলোচনা পোস্ট দেখুন - [আলোচনা পোস্টের লিঙ্ক]

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৩) Test to demonstrate anatomy of pancreas prior to surgery
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
MRCP (Magnetic Resonance Cholangiopancreatography) is a non-invasive investigation that clearly demonstrates the anatomy of the pancreatic duct and biliary tree, making it the preferred test for preoperative anatomical assessment.

Exam pearl:
MRCP → Best non-invasive imaging for pancreaticobiliary anatomy before surgery.
ERCP → Mainly therapeutic, not routine for diagnosis.


সলভ ক্লাসের জন্য আলোচনা পোস্ট দেখুন - [আলোচনা পোস্টের লিঙ্ক]

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৪) Which can confirm Achalasia of oesophagus?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Esophageal manometry is the gold standard for confirming achalasia. It demonstrates:

  • Failure of lower esophageal sphincter (LES) relaxation

  • Absent esophageal peristalsis

Exam pearl:
Gold standard for achalasia → Esophageal manometry
Barium swallow → Bird's beak appearance (suggestive, not confirmatory).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৫) GGT is mostly related to
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT) is an enzyme that is most strongly associated with chronic alcohol consumption. It is highly sensitive for alcohol-induced liver injury and is often elevated in alcoholic liver disease.

Exam pearl:
↑ GGT → Alcohol use (most characteristic association)
ALP + GGT ↑ → Suggests hepatobiliary origin of raised ALP.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৬) Gastric and duodenal ulcer can be differentiated from erosion on the basis of penetration into
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
A peptic ulcer is defined as a mucosal defect that extends through the muscularis mucosa into the deeper layers, whereas an erosion is confined to the mucosa and does not penetrate the muscularis mucosa.

Exam pearl:
Ulcer → Penetrates beyond muscularis mucosa
Erosion → Limited to mucosa, does not cross muscularis mucosa

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৭) Changes in which coagulation marker occur relatively quickly following liver damage?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Prothrombin Time (PT) changes rapidly after liver damage because Factor VII, which is synthesized in the liver, has the shortest half-life (≈4–6 hours) among the vitamin K–dependent clotting factors. Therefore, PT is the earliest and most sensitive coagulation marker of impaired hepatic synthetic function.

Exam pearl:
Earliest coagulation marker affected in liver disease → PT (due to short half-life of Factor VII).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৮) Preferred investigation in PUD
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Upper GI endoscopy (Esophagogastroduodenoscopy, EGD) is the preferred investigation for peptic ulcer disease (PUD) because it allows direct visualization of the ulcer, assessment of bleeding, biopsy to exclude malignancy (especially gastric ulcer), and testing for H. pylori.

Exam pearl:
Investigation of choice for PUD → Upper GI Endoscopy (EGD)
Gold standard for diagnosis and biopsy of gastric ulcers.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ১৯) Initial test for chronic hepatitis B
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
HBsAg (Hepatitis B surface antigen) is the initial screening test for chronic hepatitis B. Persistence of HBsAg for more than 6 months indicates chronic HBV infection. Further evaluation includes HBeAg, HBV DNA, and liver function tests.

Exam pearl:
Initial test for chronic HBV → HBsAg
HBsAg positive >6 months = Chronic hepatitis B.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২০) Most common side effect H. Pylori eradication therapy
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Diarrhoea is the most common side effect of Helicobacter pylori eradication therapy, mainly due to the use of multiple antibiotics (e.g., clarithromycin, amoxicillin, metronidazole) and proton pump inhibitors, which alter the normal intestinal flora.

Exam pearl:
Most common adverse effect of H. pylori eradication therapy → Diarrhoea
Common regimen → PPI + 2 antibiotics (± bismuth).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২১) Presentation of acute severe liver disease
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Jaundice is the most common clinical presentation of acute severe liver disease, resulting from impaired bilirubin metabolism due to hepatocellular injury.

Portal hypertension and ascites are features of chronic liver disease, while abnormal LFTs are laboratory findings rather than clinical presentation.

Exam pearl:
Acute severe liver disease → Jaundice
Chronic liver disease → Portal hypertension, Ascites, Splenomegaly

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২২) Electrolyte and acid base status in GOO can be described as
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
In gastric outlet obstruction (GOO), persistent vomiting leads to loss of gastric hydrochloric acid (HCl). This results in:

  • Loss of chloride (Cl⁻) → Hypochloraemia

  • Loss of hydrogen ions (H⁺) → Metabolic alkalosis

  • Often accompanied by hypokalaemia due to renal compensation.

Exam pearl:
GOO / Persistent vomiting → Hypochloraemic, hypokalaemic metabolic alkalosis.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৩) Most common cause of acute liver failure
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Viral hepatitis (especially Hepatitis B, with or without Hepatitis D, and Hepatitis E in endemic regions) is the most common cause of acute liver failure worldwide.
(In many Western countries, paracetamol overdose is the leading cause, but globally and in standard MBBS exams, viral hepatitis is the expected answer.)

Exam pearl:
Worldwide most common cause of acute liver failure → Viral hepatitis
Western countries → Paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৪) Triad of Zollinger-Ellison syndrome excludes
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).option2: Poor response to standard ulcer therapy
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).option4: Neuroendocrine tumour of pancreas or duodenum
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The classic triad of Zollinger–Ellison syndrome consists of:

  1. Severe/recurrent peptic ulceration

  2. Gastric acid hypersecretion

  3. Gastrinoma (neuroendocrine tumor of the pancreas or duodenum)

Although poor response to standard ulcer therapy is a common clinical feature and may raise suspicion, it is not part of the classic triad.

Exam pearl:
Zollinger–Ellison syndrome triad = Gastrinoma + Gastric acid hypersecretion + Severe/recurrent peptic ulcers.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৫) Cardinal manifestation of acute liver failure
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The cardinal manifestation of acute liver failure is hepatic encephalopathy (cerebral disturbances), resulting from the accumulation of neurotoxins (especially ammonia) due to severe hepatic dysfunction. Acute liver failure is defined by encephalopathy and coagulopathy in a patient without pre-existing chronic liver disease.

Exam pearl:
Acute liver failure = Hepatic encephalopathy + Coagulopathy (INR ≥1.5)
Cardinal feature → Cerebral disturbances (hepatic encephalopathy).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৬) All patient with functional dyspepsia must be advised for
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
All patients with functional dyspepsia should undergo non-invasive testing for Helicobacter pylori (e.g., urea breath test or stool antigen test) where appropriate. If H. pylori is detected, eradication therapy is recommended, as it may improve symptoms in some patients.

Exam pearl:
Functional dyspepsia → Test-and-treat strategy for H. pylori
Endoscopy is reserved for patients with alarm features or older age.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৭) Best screening test for acute hepatitis B infection
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
HBsAg (Hepatitis B surface antigen) is the best screening test for acute hepatitis B infection because it is the first serological marker to appear in blood after infection.

  • HBsAg → Screening test for current HBV infection (acute or chronic).

  • IgM anti-HBc → Best test to confirm acute HBV infection, especially during the "window period."

  • HBeAg → Indicates high viral replication and infectivity.

  • IgM anti-HBe → Not used as a screening test.

Exam pearl:

  • Screening for HBV infection → HBsAg

  • Confirmation of acute HBV → IgM anti-HBc

  • Window period marker → IgM anti-HBc

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৮) The area most commonly affected in abdominal TB
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The ileocaecal region is the most commonly affected site in abdominal tuberculosis because of:

  • Physiological stasis

  • Abundant lymphoid tissue (Peyer's patches)

  • Increased absorption favoring localization of Mycobacterium tuberculosis

Exam pearl:
Most common site of abdominal TB → Ileocaecal region
(Common presentations: right iliac fossa pain, abdominal mass, intestinal obstruction.)

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ২৯) Cause of major elevation of serum transaminase
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Paracetamol (acetaminophen) overdose causes massive hepatocellular necrosis, leading to a marked elevation of serum transaminases (AST/ALT), often >1000 IU/L. Such very high transaminase levels are characteristic of acute toxic or ischemic liver injury.

Exam pearl:
AST/ALT >1000 IU/L → Think:

  • Paracetamol toxicity

  • Acute viral hepatitis

  • Ischemic hepatitis ("shock liver")

Paracetamol overdose is the classic cause of massive transaminase elevation.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩০) Cardinal finding in portal hypertension
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Splenomegaly is the cardinal clinical finding of portal hypertension due to congestion of the splenic vein from increased portal venous pressure. It is a consistent sign and is often associated with hypersplenism.

Exam pearl:
Portal hypertension → Splenomegaly (cardinal sign)
Major life-threatening complication → Variceal bleeding
Common complication → Ascites

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩১) Which disease can involve any part of GIT from mouth to anus?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Crohn's disease can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from the mouth to the anus, although the terminal ileum is the most commonly involved site. It is characterized by transmural inflammation and skip lesions.

Exam pearl:

  • Crohn's disease → Mouth to anus, skip lesions, transmural inflammation

  • Ulcerative colitis → Colon only, continuous lesions, mucosal inflammation

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩২) Jaundice is usually detectable clinically when the plasma bilirubin exceeds....mg/dl
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Clinical jaundice usually becomes visible when the serum bilirubin exceeds approximately 2 mg/dL (≈34 μmol/L). The sclera is typically the first site where jaundice is noticed because of its high elastin content.

Exam pearl:
Visible jaundice → Serum bilirubin >2 mg/dL
Scleral icterus appears before skin jaundice.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৩) 1st line treatment of refractory ascites
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Refractory ascites is ascites that does not respond to sodium restriction and maximal diuretic therapy or recurs rapidly after therapeutic paracentesis. The first-line treatment is large-volume paracentesis (LVP) with intravenous albumin replacement to prevent circulatory dysfunction.

Exam pearl:

  • First-line for refractory ascites → Large-volume paracentesis + Albumin

  • TIPSS is considered in selected patients with recurrent refractory ascites who are suitable candidates.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৪) Most common site of Crohn’s disease
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The terminal ileum is the most common site affected by Crohn's disease, although the disease can involve any part of the gastrointestinal tract from the mouth to the anus. It is characterized by transmural inflammation and skip lesions.

Exam pearl:

  • Most common site of Crohn's disease → Terminal ileum

  • Crohn's disease → Mouth to anus, skip lesions, transmural inflammation

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৫) Dominant feature in obstructive jaundice
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
In obstructive jaundice, the dominant clinical feature is pruritus (itching) due to the accumulation of bile salts in the skin. Although dark urine and pale stools are common features, pruritus is the hallmark symptom of cholestasis.

Exam pearl:
Obstructive jaundice → Pruritus is the dominant symptom
Associated findings: Dark urine, pale stools, ↑ALP, ↑GGT.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৬) Which is the best means of detecting ascites?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Ultrasonography (USG) is the best initial and most sensitive investigation for detecting ascites. It can detect even small amounts of free intraperitoneal fluid (≈100 mL) and is non-invasive, readily available, and useful for guiding paracentesis.

Exam pearl:
Best investigation for detecting ascites → Ultrasonography (USG)
CT is more sensitive but is not the first-line investigation.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৭) Most common presentation in IBS
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The hallmark and most common presentation of Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) is recurrent abdominal pain or discomfort, which is typically related to defecation and associated with changes in stool frequency or stool form (Rome IV criteria).

Exam pearl:
IBS = Recurrent abdominal pain/discomfort + Altered bowel habits
Abdominal pain/discomfort is the key presenting feature.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৮) Most common cause of ascites
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Cirrhosis of the liver is the most common cause of ascites, accounting for about 80–85% of cases. Ascites develops due to portal hypertension and reduced hepatic albumin synthesis, leading to fluid accumulation in the peritoneal cavity.

Exam pearl:
Most common cause of ascites → Cirrhosis
Other causes: Malignancy, heart failure, tuberculosis, nephrotic syndrome.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৩৯) Alarm features of IBS excludes
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Female gender is not an alarm feature in Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS). In fact, IBS is more common in females.

Alarm (red flag) features that suggest an organic disease and warrant further evaluation include:

  • Weight loss

  • Iron deficiency anaemia

  • Rectal bleeding

  • Nocturnal symptoms

  • Family history of colorectal cancer/IBD

  • Onset after age 50

Exam pearl:
IBS alarm features: Weight loss, anaemia, rectal bleeding, nocturnal symptoms, age >50, family history of colorectal cancer/IBD.
Female gender is a risk factor for IBS, not an alarm feature.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪০) Cause of small liver
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Cirrhosis is the most common cause of a small, shrunken liver due to progressive fibrosis and regenerative nodule formation in the late stage of chronic liver disease.

Exam pearl:

  • Small liver → Cirrhosis (end-stage chronic liver disease)

  • Large liver → NAFLD, metastases, cysts, acute hepatitis

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪১) Osmotic laxative
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Lactulose is an osmotic laxative. It works by drawing water into the intestinal lumen, softening stool, and promoting bowel movements. It is also commonly used to treat hepatic encephalopathy by reducing ammonia absorption.

Exam pearl:

  • Osmotic laxative → Lactulose

  • Bulk-forming → Ispaghula husk

  • Stimulant laxatives → Bisacodyl, Senna

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪২) Which poison act by inactivating acetylcholinesterase (AChE)?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Organophosphorus compounds (OPCs) irreversibly inhibit acetylcholinesterase (AChE), causing accumulation of acetylcholine at muscarinic, nicotinic, and CNS synapses. This results in a cholinergic crisis.

Exam pearl:
OPC poisoning → AChE inhibition → ↑ Acetylcholine
Treatment: Atropine + Pralidoxime (2-PAM) (given early) + supportive care.

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৩) Which enzyme is more specific for hepatocellular damage?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Alanine aminotransferase (ALT) is more specific for hepatocellular injury because it is found predominantly in hepatocytes. In contrast, AST is also present in cardiac muscle, skeletal muscle, kidney, and brain, making it less liver-specific.

Exam pearl:

  • ALT → More specific for hepatocellular damage

  • AST → Less specific (also found in muscle and heart)

  • ALP & GGT → Markers of cholestasis/biliary obstruction

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৪) Charcot triad in cholangitis excludes
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
The Charcot triad of acute cholangitis consists of:

  • Fever (often with chills)

  • Jaundice

  • Right upper quadrant (RUQ) pain

Pruritus is a feature of cholestasis/obstructive jaundice, but it is not part of Charcot's triad.

Exam pearl:

  • Charcot triad: Fever + Jaundice + RUQ pain

  • Reynolds pentad: Charcot triad + Hypotension + Altered mental status (suggests severe suppurative cholangitis).

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৫) Which marker is positive in immunisation without infection by hepatitis B virus?
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
After hepatitis B vaccination, the only serological marker that becomes positive is Anti-HBs (hepatitis B surface antibody), indicating protective immunity.

  • HBsAg → Active HBV infection

  • Anti-HBc IgM → Acute HBV infection

  • Anti-HBc IgG → Previous or chronic natural infection (not produced after vaccination)

  • Anti-HBs → Immunity due to vaccination or recovery from infection

Exam pearl:
Vaccinated (no infection): Anti-HBs positive only
Recovered from natural infection: Anti-HBs + Anti-HBc IgG positive

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৬) Poor wound healing is associated with malabsorption of following except
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Poor wound healing is commonly associated with deficiencies of:

  • Protein → Impaired collagen synthesis and tissue repair

  • Vitamin C → Defective collagen formation

  • Zinc → Impaired cell proliferation and immune function

Although Vitamin A has a role in epithelial integrity and immune function, it is not a classic cause of poor wound healing in malabsorption compared with the others, making it the exception in this question.

Exam pearl:
Nutrients classically associated with poor wound healing:

  • Protein

  • Vitamin C

  • Zinc

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৭) Antidote for BDZ poisoning
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Flumazenil is the specific antidote for benzodiazepine (BDZ) poisoning. It is a competitive antagonist at the benzodiazepine binding site on the GABA-A receptor, reversing sedation.

Exam pearl:

  • BDZ poisoning → Flumazenil

  • Opioid poisoning → Naloxone

  • Organophosphate poisoning → Atropine + Pralidoxime

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৮) Permanent blindness may occur following poisoning with
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Methanol poisoning can cause permanent blindness because it is metabolized by alcohol dehydrogenase to formaldehyde and then formic acid, which is toxic to the optic nerve and retina.

Clinical features include:

  • Blurred vision, "snowfield" vision

  • Metabolic acidosis with high anion gap

  • Optic disc hyperemia → optic atrophy → permanent blindness

Exam pearl:

  • Methanol → Blindness (optic nerve toxicity)

  • Ethylene glycol → Acute kidney injury

  • Ethanol/Fomepizole → Antidotes for methanol poisoning (by blocking alcohol dehydrogenase)

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৪৯) Left iliac fossa mass may be due to
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
A left iliac fossa (LIF) mass is most commonly caused by a diverticular mass resulting from acute sigmoid diverticulitis.

  • Caecal mass → Right iliac fossa

  • Crohn's disease → Usually terminal ileum/right iliac fossa

  • Appendix abscess → Right iliac fossa

  • Diverticular mass → Left iliac fossa

Exam pearl:

  • LIF mass → Diverticular disease

  • RIF mass → Appendicular mass/abscess, Crohn's disease, Caecal carcinoma

Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).question: ৫০) Drug that can cause acute colonic pseudo-obstruction
Free Exam (Important Topic - Medicine).exp:
Opiates are a well-recognized cause of acute colonic pseudo-obstruction (Ogilvie syndrome) because they reduce colonic motility by acting on μ-opioid receptors in the gastrointestinal tract, leading to functional bowel obstruction without a mechanical cause.

Exam pearl:

  • Drug causing acute colonic pseudo-obstruction → Opiates

  • Common precipitants of Ogilvie syndrome: Recent surgery, severe illness/trauma, electrolyte disturbances, opioids, anticholinergic drugs.
